WINNER: fsd-app--A-two-depths-compacted-nbp_flash_02, 4096x4096, downsampled to 3000x3000. Replaces skingenetix-copper-peptide-serum-dropper-detail.jpg, a product shot borrowed from another page.

THIS IS THE SECOND HALF OF A PAIR. The `causes` block two rows above carries skingenetix-loss-of-skin-firmness-collagen-elastin-cross-section.jpg — the damage. This is the repair, and the two are read in sequence in the same carousel, so they share camera (square-on front elevation), block, layer stack, palette and ground.

MATCHED SYSTEM, NOT MATCHED FRAME. The composition is deliberately not the damage picture with the damage healed: two images of the identical block, one broken and one mended, is a before-and-after of the same tissue and a measured-result claim this copy does not make. Fibre courses, lobule sizes and surface contour all differ; only the style carries over.

THE TWO MECHANISMS ARE BOTH LEGIBLE, which is what settled the choice. The copy names two and the picture shows two, at two different depths:
  SUPPORT     two spheres hold a short chain of five linked pearl beads and send shafts of warm light
              STRAIGHT DOWN past the granular band into the FIBRE LAYER, where a starburst glint bursts and
              the bundles around it are thicker, brighter and lit from within, falling off with distance
  SUPPLEMENT  two more spheres hold short stubby segments of the SAME PEARL-IVORY FIBRE the scaffold is made
              of, sit down ON the quilted surface and release there only, with no shaft and no depth; the
              pads glow and sit plumper beneath them

The two actives are told apart by WHAT THEY ARE MADE OF rather than by colour — the same discipline the skin palette forced on the fibres. Verified at 100%: the bead chain reads as five beads linked in a row, the collagen segments read as short glossy fibre pieces, and neither is a loose scatter of pearls.

CLAIMS. Depicted: arrival, absorption and a local response falling off with distance — a mechanism propagating through tissue, the device established in r2 of the copper-peptide set. Not depicted: any before-and-after, comparison, number, percentage, measurement or face. NOTHING INJECTED — needle, syringe, cannula and filler were negated by name, because this is a topical product and an injectable read would be false and regulated.

NO BRAND COLOUR, matching the damage frame. Teal is Matrixyl's, Clinical blue and copper are the copper-peptide page's. This pair is generic skin: peach-cream tissue, pearl-ivory fibre, pale cool grey-white haze, and the only bright thing in frame is the warm white light of the delivery itself.

Also checked at 100%: the fibre bundles are whole and their cut ends at the block face are solid, not the open bores that disqualified nbp_pro_01 on the damage frame.

SQUARE, 1:1, NON-NEGOTIABLE — the row height in `media-with-text` is set by the master's own aspect, so a non-square file would make this block taller than its siblings.

NEW FILENAME, never a re-upload: Shopify Files suffixes a name collision and keeps serving the original. ALT TEXT describes the illustration as an illustration and claims no result.

BACKGROUND REGRADED TO MATCH THE DAMAGE FRAME, Malcolm 2026-08-26: 'can we adjust the background of the second image to match the color of the first image?'. The render came back on a cool grey-white ground (R-B about -6 across the frame) against the causes frame's warm cream (R-B about +25). Side by side down the page the temperature shift was visible.

HOW, because the obvious method leaves blotches. A flood fill from the frame edges gives a clean background mask that correctly excludes the block and the spheres, and a per-channel mean/standard-deviation match onto the causes background warms it. But the flood stops at soft halos, so two grey patches survived in the upper right — background the fill could not reach, left cool while everything around it went warm, which looked worse than the original mismatch.

The fix is a second, colour-based term unioned into the mask: ANY COOL PIXEL IS BACKGROUND THE FLOOD MISSED. The target ground is warm everywhere and nothing in this tissue is cool, so `B - R > 0`, feathered, catches the leftovers exactly. It also catches the glass highlights in the spheres and gives them a little warmth, which is correct — they sit in the same ambient. Verified afterwards: R-B now runs +20 to +25 across the frame against the target's +12 to +34, and zero pixels anywhere are cool.

Regraded in place from the published master rather than re-generated, so the frame Malcolm approved is byte-for-byte the same picture with a different ground. Uploaded under a new filename for the Shopify Files reason above; the cool-ground file stays uploaded but unreferenced.

GLOW AT THE TOPICAL CONTACT POINTS, Malcolm 2026-08-26: 'add more glow effect of the topical peptides touching the outer layer of skin'. The two collagen-segment spheres sit on the quilted surface but their contact read faintly against the two deep starbursts below. Contact points measured off a coordinate grid overlaid on the master rather than eyeballed — (0.660, 0.330) and (0.810, 0.330) in fractional coords. A three-lobe warm-white bloom is screen-blended at each: a tight core at the contact, a wider bloom spreading into the pads, and a low flat wash running along the surface. Strength chosen AT RENDER SIZE, not at 100%: this block draws at 660px on the page, and the version that looked right full-size was timid there. Three strengths were rendered at 660px and the middle one (core 0.50) won — it balances the two deep glints without flattening the quilted pads, which the stronger settings did.

GREY SHAPES IN THE BOTTOM GAP REMOVED, same day: 'remove the grey colored shapes at the bottom - between the glass floor - and the lowest layer of skin orbs'. Worth recording that these were in the ORIGINAL nbp_flash render, not introduced by the regrade — the glass plate and the gap above it came back at around R199 G187 B185, a near-neutral grey, sitting against a cream ground at R238 G218 B206. FIRST ATTEMPT WAS WRONG: a horizontal blur inside the band, meant to average the mottled shapes away, smeared the orb bellies into mush and did not touch the grey at all. What works is targeting by SATURATION, not by shape: inside a feathered band from y 0.876 to 0.964, pixels with saturation under about 34 are pushed onto the ground's own warm ratio at 1.06x luminance. The orbs sit at saturation 40-90 so they are untouched; the glass and the gap are the only things caught. Low-warmth pixels in the bottom band fall from 12.4% to 0.17%.
